title: Front Desk/Medical Receptionist
description:
Performs all necessary receptionist duties including answering, screening, and routing of phone calls. Utilizes (EMR) and/or other systems for check-in/check-out processes including verifying patient demographics, insurance information, obtaining patient signatures on applicable patient forms, and having the patient complete any paperwork associated with the visit. Collect any necessary payments and process accordingly. Facilitate patient flow by notifying the provider of patient’s arrival, delays, or backlogs. Schedule patient appointments and remind the patients of any necessary documentation that may be required for their appointment. Schedules any services or procedures as needed. Obtains/retrieves referrals/authorizations/eligibility verification that may be required. Keeps office supplies adequately stocked by anticipating inventory needs and placing orders or advising office manager of items needed. Ensures HIPAA guidelines are always followed. Provides additional coverage for night hours and weekend, as needed. Regularly required to communicate with patients, staff, and medical providers.

Excellent communication and analytical skills. Attention to detail. Ability to meet deadlines. Self-directed and self-motivated. Able to multi-task. Professional phone etiquette.

Requirements: High School diploma/GED. Graduate of an accredited Medical Office Administration program or at least 6 months of prior experience working as a Medical Receptionist or 1 year of clerical experience. Microsoft Office proficiency.

title: Independent Living Specialist
description:
DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:
Responsible for all aspects of assigned caseload, including meeting with clients living in Community Residence as needed but at least weekly. Make referrals to medical, mental health and/or substance abuse services as needed, and continue to involve providers in the clients care. Provide clients with supportive counseling. Make regular visits to client room, and monitor clients to ensure a safe and secure environment. Teach and assist clients with activities of daily living. Complete client 2010 e housing applications, service plans, and psychosocial reports. Provide appropriate level of support including escorts if necessary for client. Ensure that all clinical files and reports are complete and up to date. Assist with intake and admission process. Participate in community meetings. Provide emergency first aid/CPR assistance when needed. Related duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:
BA preferred. HS diploma/ GED required and significant experience working with the substance abuse and/or mentally ill population required. Excellent writing skills. Basic computer literacy required. CPR training certification or willingness to take training class in CPR.
